chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Elmer Fain, bandleader who could not play
summary: Howard says Fain always led bands but could not play alto sax well or read, and he would never hire him.

bands.name: Elmer Fain and his Musical Bees

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah, you wouldn't know about. Anyway, nearly 3,000 of all races attended the drag ball. Many of Hollywood's best-known (unintelligible) were in beautiful costumes, and so on. Some had gone to considerable expense and so on. Yeah, but, anyway, this is from 1934 or 5. Who knows who can remember that far back?
Oh, no.
But, anyway, we see where Elmer Fain was a bandleader, too. You forgot to tell me that.
He's always been a band leader.
Really?
Ever since he's been in the union.
But what was his instrument? I didn't know Fain played anything.
He can't play.
He can't play?
No. (laughter)
But what instrument was he attempting to play?
Played an alto sax.
Alto sax.
He tried to play.
Did he ever work with your band?
No.
No, huh?
No, sir, no. I wouldn't have him.
I know what you mean. But, anyway, that was interesting.
It's just like if you had a band, you wouldn't -- there's certain people you wouldn't have.
I would not hire them if they couldn't play. Do you think he was a good reader?
Who, Fain?
Fain, yeah.
No. I'll be honest with you.
